rankingReason: i liked both the IME and CRULP a lot. I have prior experience with the CRULP, so part of is that I'm used to it. But it also seems intuitive to match the urdu letters to the english sounds. I think the reality is that most people type Urdu in romanized letters quite often while texting, so this system takes advantage of that. I didn't think I would like the IME, but it was surprisingly intuitive, and it took the "texting Urdu" to another level by making it easier to type roman and have it come out as Urdu. It was definitely clunky around certain Urdu sounds that aren't always pronounced, like 'ain, or around words that are borrowed into Urdu like "Iliad." But overall it was surprisingly easy to use. The windows one is good in theory, but because of the dominance of romanized Urdu in my personal use, it's too much of an initial input to learn the placement of the letters. It may work better for someone who uses Romanized Urdu less in their daily life.

I prefer the Roman keyboard the most because I usually type Urdu with the English keyboard, so writing that way and being able to choose the correct Urdu word I mean is convenient and easy.
